item.text:
Initial read: 2024 looked mixed. Marcos projected a reformist, pro-investment, and security-forward presidency, but the year was also defined by rice-price pressure, West Philippine Sea friction, and softer public approval than at the start of the year. I could not verify the repository’s exact sub-ID taxonomy in this isolated pass, so I am tagging claims with broad chapter-level IDs only.

| Context | Source | Claim-level summary | Broad question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 event, favorable | [PBBM ushers Filipinos to a “Bagong Pilipinas” that serves its people](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-bagong-pilipinas-that-serves-its-people/) — Presidential Communications Office, January 28, 2024 | Marcos opened the year by framing 2024 as a governance-reform push: stronger execution, more responsive government, and a “Bagong Pilipinas” brand of administration. This is evidence of the term’s self-presentation and policy direction, not proof of delivery. | `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, favorable | [PBBM: PH acts to protect national interest, maintains independent foreign policy](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ph-acts-to-protect-national-interest-maintains-independent-foreign-policy/) — Presidential Communications Office, March 4, 2024 | Marcos publicly emphasized an independent foreign policy while defending Philippine interests amid South China Sea tensions. This shows a clear 2024 diplomatic posture. | `7D.*`, `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, favorable / civic space | [PBBM declares free, safe environment for journalists under Bagong Pilipinas](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/) — Presidential Communications Office, April 15, 2024 | Marcos pledged press freedom and journalist safety in a high-profile public event. Useful as official intent, though it should be weighed against independent press-freedom concerns below. | `7C.*`, `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, critical | [Philippines needs to ‘do more’ than protest China’s actions in South China Sea, Marcos says](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-needs-to-do-more-than-protest-chinas-actions-in-south-china-sea-marcos-says/2149370/) — Reuters/ThePrint, June 27, 2024 | After a violent June 17 maritime confrontation, Marcos said the Philippines needed more than protests. This is strong evidence that the West Philippine Sea remained a major operational and security stressor in 2024. | `7D.*`, `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, critical | [Marcos opens 2024 SONA admitting rice prices are costly](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914278/marcos-opens-2024-sona-admitting-rice-prices-are-costly/story/) — GMA News Online, July 22, 2024 | Marcos acknowledged in his SONA that high rice prices were a real pain point for Filipinos. This is one of the clearest 2024 indicators that cost-of-living pressures undercut the administration’s macro narrative. | `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, mixed | [June 2024 Nationwide Survey on the Performance and Trustworthiness Ratings of the Top Philippine Government Officials](https://pulseasia.ph/updates/june-2024-nationwide-survey-on-the-performance-and-trustworthiness-ratings-of-the-top-philippine-government-officials/) — Pulse Asia Research, July 17, 2024 | Pulse Asia’s June survey showed Marcos at 53% approval and 52% trust, down from March, but still majority-positive. This is good evidence of a weakening but still viable public mandate mid-year. | `8A.*`, `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, mixed / favorable | [Marcos net satisfaction rating up in June — SWS](https://tribune.net.ph/amp/story/2024/08/02/marcos-net-satisfaction-rating-up-in-june-sws) — Tribune / reporting SWS, August 2, 2024 | SWS found 55% satisfied, 28% dissatisfied, net +27 in June 2024, an improvement from March. This is a counterweight to the Pulse Asia softness and suggests the term was not uniformly unpopular. | `8A.*`, `8B.*` |
| 2024 event, critical / background on civic space | [Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) — Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, June 17, 2024 | The country report says the Marcos government was more media-friendly than Duterte’s, but press-freedom concerns persisted: red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and continuing threats against journalists. This is useful background on the civic-space environment during 2024. | `7C.*` |
| 2024 event, favorable / granular performance | [SWS survey: PBBM ‘very good’ on helping disaster victims, improving children’s quality of education, helping the poor](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/) — Presidential Communications Office, September 14, 2024 | The administration highlighted SWS findings that Marcos scored strongly on disaster response, education, and aid to the poor. This supports a more favorable reading of administrative competence in specific service-delivery areas. | `8B.*` |

Short synthesis: the 2024 record looks like a presidency that was still politically viable and able to claim some policy successes, but one under pressure on prices, maritime security, and civic-space credibility. The strongest positive evidence is about intent and selective performance; the strongest negative evidence is about rice affordability, South China Sea incidents, and media-freedom concerns.
